paper_metadata.title: Prompt Me One More Time: A Two-Step Knowledge Extraction Pipeline with Ontology-Based Verification
paper_metadata.venue: Proceedings of TextGraphs-17: Graph-based Methods for Natural Language Processing
paper_metadata.abstract: The study proposes a two-step LLM pipeline for extending Wikidata: first extract triplet candidates, then refine and link entities and relations to canonical KG names, and finally verify triples with Wikidata relation constraints. It compares the pipeline with a model fine-tuned on machine-generated data and reports better performance on natural data.

paper_metadata-abstract-04-01.excerpt: We propose a two-step pipeline that includes the initial extraction of entity candidates, followed by their refinement and linkage to the canonical entities and relations of the knowledge graph. problem_addressed: How to extend Wikidata from unstructured text with accurate, canonical Wikidata triples without training a separate extractor for each evolving KG or ontology. The work targets error-prone entity/relation normalization and LLM hallucinations after extraction.

methodology.description: Execution pipeline: (1) prompt gpt-3.5-turbo to emit JSON subject–relation–object candidate triples from text, using in-context examples; (2) use a FAISS dense-retrieval index built from pretrained Contriever embeddings to retrieve the top five similar canonical Wikidata names for every candidate subject, relation, and object; (3) prompt the LLM again to choose context-appropriate canonical names only from each retrieved list and output refined JSON triples; (4) query Wikidata type hierarchies and apply the extracted relation's subject and value constraints, retaining a triple only when subject and object hierarchy types align with those constraints.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: Wikidata supplies the target KG ontology, canonical entity and relation names, subject/value property constraints, and P31 ('instance of') and P279 ('subclass of') type hierarchies. Verification is post-processing: it filters triples inconsistent with relation constraints; the ontology is not supplied in the refinement prompt because that would make it unreasonably large.

input_output.input_type: Unstructured natural-language text, including SynthIE synthetic texts and manually sampled Wikipedia paragraphs.
input_output.input_granularity: Individual text instances/short passages; the natural-language evaluation uses paragraphs, while prompts accept a single item labelled 'Text'.
input_output.output_representation: A JSON list of verified subject–relation–object triples whose names are canonical Wikidata entity and relation names; triples failing ontology consistency checks are removed.

models_and_tools: SPARQL queries over P31 and P279
datasets: Wiki-cIE Code training split (source of in-context examples)
WikicIE-test-small (100 random samples used to select matched Wikipedia paragraphs)
Natural Language corpora: 100 manually sampled Wikipedia paragraphs

metrics: Mean and standard deviation over three runs with different in-context examples
Intersection over union (IoU) of correct triples between models
baselines: SynthIE T5-large, reported as the best-reported model trained on SynthIE and fine-tuned on SynthIE-text-small
evaluation.setting: Ablation study on SynthIE-text-small compares the full pipeline with removal of verification, refinement, and in-context examples; results use three runs with different in-context example sets. The main comparison evaluates the full pipeline and SynthIE T5-large on SynthIE-text-small, then uses human evaluation on 100 matched natural-language Wikipedia paragraphs. Three paper authors independently label predicted triples as text-consistent; a triple is correct when at least two agree. Natural-language correctness includes facts explicitly stated, implied, or readily derivable without additional knowledge.

value: On SynthIE-text-small, the full pipeline achieved F1 0.55±0.01, precision 0.59±0.03, and recall 0.52±0.005.

Removing verification gave F1 0.53±0.01, precision 0.55±0.03, recall 0.52±0.005; removing refinement gave F1 0.51±0.01, precision 0.60±0.03, recall 0.44±0.006. Without in-context examples, F1 was 0.16, precision 0.65, recall 0.09.
On SynthIE-text-small, fine-tuned SynthIE T5-large scored F1 0.88, precision 0.87, recall 0.88, versus the proposed pipeline's 0.55/0.59/0.52.
On the human-evaluated natural-language corpus, the proposed method had precision 0.74 with 187 correct triples, versus 0.55 and 201 for SynthIE T5-large; correct-triple IoU was 0.08.

value: The pipeline requires no task-specific fine-tuning and can normalize open-text extractions to canonical Wikidata names through retrieval plus a second prompt.

Refinement materially improves recall in the reported ablation (0.44 without refinement to 0.52 full pipeline), while ontology filtering improves precision after refinement (0.55 without verification to 0.59 full pipeline).
The method has higher human-evaluated precision than the fine-tuned SynthIE baseline on the paper's matched natural-language Wikipedia set (0.74 versus 0.55).

value: REVIEW-LEVEL INFERENCE (not an author claim): Candidate normalization is constrained to the retriever's top-five names; therefore, a correct Wikidata entity or relation absent from that shortlist cannot be selected in the second prompting step.

REVIEW-LEVEL INFERENCE (not an author claim): The ontology check tests type compatibility, so it can reject ill-typed triples but does not by itself establish that a type-compatible triple is textually entailed.

The pipeline has markedly lower synthetic-data F1 than the fine-tuned SynthIE T5-large baseline (0.55 versus 0.88), and the authors note that specialized fine-tuned models may outperform it in narrow domains with adequate resources.

value: Reliable, scalable evaluation data for Wikidata triple extraction remains unresolved: the paper describes existing distant/synthetic datasets as sparse, noisy, or inconsistent with their texts.
Generalization across source-text and KG domains remains unresolved because the method can require manual prompt/domain adaptation.

REVIEW-LEVEL INFERENCE (not an author claim): The work does not establish recall over all facts in real-world text, because its natural-language evaluation reports human-judged precision and number of correct outputs rather than a complete gold set of all extractable triples.
